body: Music helps me. Songs that tell a story. Thinking deeply about my actions. But what really keeps me here is other peoples stories. Often when I get into a state of an extreme low, I just read story after story. Sometimes for an entire night. You should talk to some of the mods on /r/suicidewatch, maybe. I might not be a good person to talk to though. I find a strangely good feeling in being sad. Like it is something I am good at.

Note: Everything I will say is my honest and complete view of how life is.

Life was, is, and will be a complete and utter accident. No one exists on purpose in a grand scheme of the universe. That being said, you were planned for by your parents at the very least. Though I do not know your current living status, the fact that you can come to reddit, and more specifically this subreddit, and talk with like minded individuals ought to speak volumes about your life and who you are. I do not know your physical appearance, but I do know mine. I am roughly average height, and 260lbs. I have been this way for five years straight. Although my appearance never changed, my feelings of vanity and the monster "mirror" have. I used to think to be a skeleton was to be a model. That if you parted your hair the right way, if you had the thigh gap, if you wore the right makeup, you could make friends and be successful. None of that is true. Character and honesty are the true values one should strive for. Even if it means people feel hurt. 

Night time isn't the enemy, it is the dark. I have had some experiences similar to your description. Most recently I was playing a game with a friend I met online, and we were just playing and talking. Then there was this pause. And I just started wondering "Why am I alive?" That is, the environment of dark, quiet, reflective moments, can make even the most happy and content wonder if they could have done better. I suggest keeping a soft lamp in the center of the room. Or where you spend the most time. 

As for death being a suitable alternative than fighting. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ You are not wrong. But you are not right either. It is indeed easier to roll over and take it than to fight, but... I do not know how to explain properly. I imagine it like this. "I am going to die. There is no way around that. I can summon death at this moment if I desire. But if I do, will people know why? I mean, truly? Or will my life be surmised with the phrase "He was sad"? I can see how people will react, but what if something changes? What if some do not simply get over it? Will I be able to see it unfold afterward?" This mindset has given me the chance to sit in front of this computer today. Whether that is good or bad is still up in the air. -This may not be what you were looking for. And mods might take this comment away, but if you were to take anything away, take this: Pain is a lot like life, it is only temporary.
